sampling_model.design: Population-level finite SCM identification from the full observed law with \(G,\Omega,W,\Pi,x,y\) supplied to the decision problem; no experimental randomization is assumed.
sampling_model.units: The identification statements compare all finite SCMs inducing the same observed distribution; sampling enters only after identification.
sampling_model.treatment: The intervention replaces the equations at \(X\) by the fixed assignment \(x\).
sampling_model.overlap: The novel input \(\Pi\) declares arbitrary positive or zero observed events. It is distinct from Chen--Darwiche Theorem 15's separability and parent conditions and from Theorem 18's treatment-marginal positivity set \(C_V=\{\Pr(X)>0:X\text{ is a treatment variable}\}\); only denominators executed on a support branch must be certified positive.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Not part of the kernel; a multinomial plug-in estimator is available after a guarded formula is returned.

body.tldr: The paper asks for a complete support-aware analogue of the ID algorithm, \(\operatorname{FID\text{-}S}(G,\Omega,W,\Pi,x,y)\), for finite latent DAGs with supplied observed alphabets, qualitative functional nodes, and declared positive or zero observed events. Its bounded partial-trace grammar must either refute the declarations, derive a guarded formula for \(P_x(y)\), or lift a local obstruction to two exact-support rational SCMs with the same observed law while preserving \(\Omega\) and the latent-source architecture of \(G\): exactly the root vertices and parent incidences of \(G\), model-specific finite latent alphabets, and sourcewise independence in each model, without shared root masses across the pair. Each existentially constructed rational witness uses individually reduced primitive root and conditional-table fractions, not an unspecified common denominator, with derived latent-cardinality and serialized bit bounds, and has a witness-dependent target separation \(\Delta>0\) rather than an absolute gap guarantee. Finite terminal-certificate syntax, decidable rule checking, and explicit checker and search bounds are obligations of the open grammar construction. The supported-bow pattern \(\mathcal B_0\) is the first explicit case beyond ordinary ID, Chen--Darwiche Theorem 15 functional-variable elimination under its separability and parent conditions, and Theorem 18's treatment-marginal positivity set \(C_V=\{\Pr(X)>0:X\text{ is a treatment variable}\}\). It also lies outside Chen--Darwiche's 2026 sound state-based algorithms, whose inputs are context-specific independences and state-alphabet constraints under a strictly positive observational law, because \(\mathcal B_0\) retains intervention state \(A=1\) in \(\Omega_A\) while declaring \(P(A=1)=0\). The declared support-literal regime is likewise outside the positive-observational-law scope of the sound-and-complete gID result of Kivva, Mokhtarian, Etesami, and Kiyavash. The genuinely open content is exhaustive search termination, finite grammar and certificate construction, the general latent lift, converse formula reconstruction, and associated complexity bounds.

project_justification.gap: Ordinary hedge completeness ignores declared structural-zero faces. Chen--Darwiche Theorem 15 gives functional-variable elimination under stated separability and parent conditions, and Theorem 18 assumes the treatment-marginal positivity set \(C_V=\{\Pr(X)>0:X\text{ is a treatment variable}\}\); neither theorem identifies the arbitrary declared zero-and-positive support-literal regime introduced here. Chen--Darwiche's 2026 Theorems 1--2 are sound formula-returning algorithms for state-based effects under context-specific independences and state-alphabet constraints with a strictly positive observational law, not a complete formula-or-exact-support-countermodel procedure for valid intervention states on structural-zero faces. Kivva, Mokhtarian, Etesami, and Kiyavash prove sound-and-complete gID under positivity of the observational law, not on arbitrary declared support faces, and do not supply exact-support rational paired witnesses. Tikka--Hyttinen--Karvanen Theorem 5 supplies a terminating sound CSI search, and Theorem 6 shows why contextwise answers do not give completeness.
project_justification.niche: Finite categorical latent SCMs with explicit observed alphabets admit combinatorial support certificates and canonical response coordinates, but existing tools do not coordinate them with query-specific hedge traces, exact witness lifting that preserves the latent-source architecture of \(G\), and auditable rational serialization.
project_justification.fill: A terminating \(\operatorname{FID\text{-}S}(G,\Omega,W,\Pi,x,y)\) procedure will preserve \(\Omega\), support, functional-row provenance, and the latent-source architecture of \(G\) through recursion and certify every terminal outcome with a guarded formula, a contradiction, or a rational separating pair obeying explicit primitive and total bit bounds. The grammar construction must also provide finite certificate syntax, decidable rule checking, and explicit checker and search complexity bounds.

body.related_work: Shpitser and Pearl supply recursive district decomposition and classical parity hedge pairs; the present kernel requires every pair to preserve the declared exact support, supplied observed alphabets, fixed functional rows, and the latent-source architecture of \(G\), with no shared root-mass requirement. Shpitser's correction ties an obstruction to the actual failed query. Chen and Darwiche's Theorem 15 gives functional-variable elimination under its stated separability and parent conditions. Their Theorem 18 instead assumes the treatment-marginal positivity set \(C_V=\{\Pr(X)>0:X\text{ is a treatment variable}\}\). Neither theorem identifies the declared support-literal regime \(\Pi\), a new input here that may include arbitrary marginal or joint zeros. Chen and Darwiche's separate constrained-identifiability work gives arithmetic-circuit invariant-cut tests for constraints including logical and \(0\)--\(1\) restrictions, but not a complete procedure for the present arbitrary support-literal and functional class or an exact-support rational-countermodel trichotomy. Chen and Darwiche's 2026 Proposition 1 shows that state-based and variable-based identification coincide with only a graph and observed law, while Theorems 1--2 give sound formula-returning algorithms after adding context-specific independences and state-alphabet constraints; the paper assumes a strictly positive observational law and does not claim completeness under those additional constraints. Its state constraints specify admissible variable states, whereas \(\Pi\) can retain \(a\in\Omega_A\) as an intervention value while declaring \(P(A=a)=0\). On \(\mathcal B_0\), ordinary ID fails on the latent bow, Theorem 15 elimination of the functional node \(D\) leaves that bow, Theorem 18 is unavailable because \(\Pr(A=1)=0\), and the 2026 algorithms' strict-positivity input excludes the support face, yet the supported query equals \(P(B=b)\) and the unsupported query has an exact rational separating pair. Hwang, Choe, Kwon, and Lee inform the tracking of formula-specific positive denominators. Tikka, Hyttinen, and Karvanen's NeurIPS 2019 Theorem 5 proves termination and soundness of their CSI search, and Theorem 6 proves that identification in every context-specific DAG need not combine to global identification; these results motivate provenance-preserving branching but are not completeness comparators. Mokhtarian, Jamshidi, Etesami, and Kiyavash obtain completeness for observed-root control contexts. Kivva, Mokhtarian, Etesami, and Kiyavash prove a sound-and-complete gID result under positivity of the observational law; it neither handles arbitrary declared support faces nor supplies exact-support rational paired witnesses, so it informs the positive-law boundary rather than serving as an extension claim. Fraser informs the support-consistency branch. Rosset, Gisin, and Wolfe give sourcewise cardinality bounds, while Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim and Duarte and coauthors give finite response and polynomial coordinates; none converts every causal obstruction into an exact-support rational separating pair with the encoding required here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The fully observed completion argument does not survive marginalization: equality of observed laws becomes a system of polynomial equalities in products of latent-source probabilities, so a local target-varying direction need not factor into independent sources. A real separating fiber also need not contain a rational point. These are the two obligations of Open-ended Question 1, not assumptions of the proposal.
body.honest_scope: The finite support oracle, supported-bow separation, and fully observed completion frontier are derived but remain to be independently proved. Exhaustive search termination, the finite latent obstruction grammar and terminal-certificate syntax, decidable checking with explicit checker and search bounds, extension preserving the latent-source architecture of \(G\), converse formula reconstruction, existence of rational separating pairs in the stated individual-fraction encoding, and explicit functions \(H(L)\) and \(B_{\mathrm{rat}}(L)\) are open. A separating witness must have \(\Delta>0\), but the gap may depend on the obstructed instance and witness; no absolute gap constant is claimed. Generic real quantifier elimination, unrestricted latent flattening, and the fully observed special case do not count as resolutions of the latent headline.
